keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Khasso row). The kingdom "straddled both banks of the upper Senegal River, from roughly Kayes to Bafoulabe", "a strip at most 60 km wide" (now Mali's Kayes Region); Séga Doua's authority reached "as far as Gajaaga" in the early reign (undated). The page also says the kingdom split into five smaller states around 1800: the shape is held to 1880 because the page does not draw the smaller states.

ledger.note: 1681: Khasso is founded. "The Fula won independence at the Battle of Toumbifara in 1681" and "elected Séga Doua (r. 1681 - 1725), Yamadou's son, as the first fankamala, or king, of Khasso"; Fula immigration is dated "before 1600" in the infobox. The overlord is not named in the extract.

ledger.note: 1880: Khasso passes to France. "Khasso was assimilated into French Sudan in 1880" (infobox: incorporation 1880). Earlier, in November 1854 Umar Tall conquered Bambuk and Khasso's petty kings submitted; Umar was repulsed at Medina Fort in 1857; in September 1855 Faidherbe built a fort at Médine and extended French protection.

notes:
Khasso, additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Page: Khasso (one page).

The page gives no founding year beyond Toumbifara (1681) and Fula immigration "before 1600"; the overlord defeated in 1681 is not named in the text read. The kingdom split into five smaller states around 1800 (Kouniakary was sacked by Kaarta, undated); the shape is held whole to 1880 with the split recorded as a ledger event at confidence 2 and no successors, because the page names none. Umar Tall's conquest (November 1854) makes the Khasso kings Tukulor subjects until 1857 on this page; the tukulor-empire dossier does not carry Khasso (page not read for it). The French protectorate of September 1855 belongs in the french-africa ledger (vassal_start 1855). The 60 km strip is the page's.
